sections.heading: $ what_is_this
sections.body: HiveScope Chat is a decentralized chat linked to Hive accounts, built on the Nostr protocol. Every message is a Nostr event, stored by hivescope-relay — there's no company account or password, your identity is a cryptographic key.

sections.heading: $ hive_keychain
sections.body: Hive Keychain is a browser extension (or mobile app) that holds your Hive keys, so you never type a password into this site or any other. You need it installed before you can link an account here — search "Hive Keychain" in your browser's extension store, or install the Hive Keychain mobile app.

sections.heading: $ linking
sections.body: Linking signs a short message once with your Hive posting key, proving you control that account. We never see or store your private key, only that one signature. Each browser/device gets its own separate link — the same Hive account can be linked from several devices at once. The "logout" button forgets this device's link; there's no export/import yet, so logging out is one-way — linking again on this browser creates a new, separate link, not a return to the old one.

sections.heading: $ rooms
sections.body: Any linked account can create a room; whoever creates a given name first becomes its owner. From then on, only that room's owner, the account currently listed as its admin (from any of your devices linked to that same Hive account), or the relay's operator account can rename it or hand off admin to someone else — but any linked account can still post in any room, room names aren't reserved for particular people to write in. Every room has a direct link (chat.hivescope.xyz/r/room-name) you can copy with the "copy link" button inside the room; opening it takes you straight there once you're linked. The link stops working when the room expires.

sections.heading: $ room_list
sections.body: Each room in the list shows how many people are online in it (the people icon), how many messages it holds, and — if you've been away — a "N new" badge with the messages you haven't seen (plus an @ badge when some mention you or reply to you); the browser tab title carries the total, like "(3) HiveScope Chat". "Seen" is remembered per device, and your own messages never count. With two or more rooms you get a search box and can sort by last activity, people online, message count or name.

sections.heading: $ mentions_replies
sections.body: Type @ and an account name to mention someone (click a sender's name to insert it, or suggestions come from people who wrote or are in the room; Tab or Enter picks one). Mentions are highlighted, and a message that mentions you or replies to yours is marked and shows an @ badge in the room list. The "reply" link under each message quotes it above yours. It's all part of the public message, so mentions and who you reply to are visible to anyone, like the rest. Below the message box you'll see "@name is typing…" while someone in the room is writing (it uses the same ephemeral presence signal, so it's public and stored nowhere). The "alerts" switch in the top bar turns on browser notifications for those mentions and replies while the tab is in the background (asks permission once; works only while the app is open, there is no push). If your browser has a built-in translator (recent desktop Chrome or Edge), other people's messages get a "translate" link that translates them into the app's language on your device — the text isn't sent anywhere; the first time, the browser may download a language pack. It doesn't appear in browsers without that feature. Links (http/https) in messages are clickable and open in a new tab; messages can be up to 2000 characters. Use the ☺+ button on a message to react with one of six emojis (👍 ❤️ 😂 🎉 😮 😢); the counts show under the message and count each Hive account once. Click your own reaction to remove it — also from another of your devices. Reactions are public, like messages.

sections.heading: $ expiration
sections.body: Whoever creates or edits a room picks how long it lasts (1 hour, 24 hours, 7, 30, or 90 days) — once that time passes with no updates, the room and its messages are removed (cleanup runs every few minutes, so a room can linger a few minutes past its mark). Renaming it, or any other edit, resets the clock from that moment with whatever duration you pick then — there's no separate "renew" action, editing is enough. Each room in the list shows how long it has left, next to its admin.

sections.heading: $ hive_snaps
sections.body: When you create a room, HiveScope offers to share it on Hive as a short "snap" — a reply to the daily @peak.snaps thread. Nothing is posted unless you press the button, then Hive Keychain asks you to sign. A snap is a real, permanent Hive post that can't be deleted, even if the room expires in an hour. The room is created either way.

sections.heading: $ theme
sections.body: Dark (the default) or light, switchable any time with the sun/moon button in the corner — your choice is remembered on this device.

sections.heading: $ privacy
sections.body: Messages are public: they're Nostr events anyone running a Nostr client can read, along with the room name and the pubkey that sent them. This isn't private or encrypted messaging — don't post anything you wouldn't want public. You can delete your own messages from any device linked to your Hive account with the "delete" link next to them: the relay removes them and they vanish for everyone in the room, but a message is public the moment it's sent, so anyone who already saw or saved it keeps their copy. The online counter (the people icon) shows how many Hive accounts are connected right now, in total and in each room — click it to see who they are: while you're linked, your browser announces every few seconds which room you're in, so anyone using the app can tell you're online and where. Nothing is stored. Profile pictures next to names are loaded from Hive's public image service (images.hive.blog), so that service can see your IP address when your browser fetches them.
